title.en: C'était: looking back at how things were

summary.en: Step from present 'it is' to past 'it was' in one word.

body.en:
From season 1, episodes 1, 5 and 6.

When the gate bell rings twice, Claire asks *C'était quoi, cette cloche?*. Later in the week, Antoine admits *C'était mon plan*, and Thibault realises *c'était toi* from the very start. Here familiar *c'est* shifts into the past using *était*, an imperfect form of *être*.

French uses *c'était* to describe a past state, identity, or background situation ('it was', 'that was') rather than a sudden action. Elided *ce* joins straight onto *était* in one smooth two-syllable unit (/setɛ/).

Learn *c'était* alongside *c'est* as a pair: present situation *c'est calme*, past impression *c'était calme*.

On replay, notice how speakers pair *c'était* with a completed action in the same breath, contrasting background with event.
